input.claim_text: On 3 February 2023 heavy rain caused the creek behind our property to overflow and water came into our home, ruining the carpets in the living room and soaking the bottom of the plasterboard walls. It happened really fast, within about an hour the water was ankle deep inside. We've had to rip up the carpet already because it started smelling. I think it'll cost around $9,000 to fix the flooring and walls.

output.cause: creek overflowed due to heavy rain
output.damaged_item: living room carpets and plasterboard walls

input.query: Flood damage from creek overflow coverage and exclusions

turns.text:
DECISION: approve

The claim describes flood damage caused by a creek overflowing its banks due to heavy rain, which meets RAA's Contents PDS definition of "Flood" — "the covering of normally dry land by water that has escaped or been released from the normal confines of ... any river, creek or other natural watercourse" [RAA Contents PDS, page 87], and this peril is explicitly covered: "loss or damage to the Insured Property provided as a result of Flood" [RAA Contents PDS, page 50].

None of the listed exclusions apply to this claim: the damage is to carpets and plasterboard walls (not pools, tanks, paths, driveways, greenhouses, or wharves), there's no indication the damage was from hydrostatic groundwater rather than surface floodwater, and there's clear structural damage (soaked plasterboard) accompanying the loss, so the paint-only exclusion is not applicable [RAA Contents PDS, page 50, page 88].

Policy figures for this policyholder: excess = $500, coverage limit = $45,000. On a claimed amount of $9,000, the calculated payout is $9,000 − $500 excess = **$8,500**, well within the coverage limit.

Sources cited:
[RAA Contents PDS, page 87]
[RAA Contents PDS, page 50]
[RAA Contents PDS, page 88]
